entities.summary:
John Henry of Luxembourg, a member of the House of Luxembourg, was Count of Tyrol from 1335 to 1341 and Margrave of Moravia from 1349 until his death.

As a key figure in the medieval politics of Central Europe, John Henry played a significant role in the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the various duchies and margraviates of the region.

His tenure as Count of Tyrol and Margrave of Moravia coincided with a period of significant cultural, economic, and military transformation in the region, including the rise of the city-states of Italy and the expansion of the Ottoman Empire.

Despite his relatively minor status in the grand narrative of medieval European history, John Henry's legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the House of Luxembourg on the politics and nobility of the region for centuries to come.

As a testament to the enduring power of medieval dynasties, John Henry's descendants continued to play important roles in shaping the course of European history, including the reign of Charles IV, Holy Roman Emperor, who was a member of the same House of Luxembourg.

The legacy of John Henry of Luxembourg can also be seen in the rich cultural heritage of the region, including the beautiful Gothic architecture of the Tyrolean and Moravian castles, which bear testament to his legacy as a patron of the arts and architecture.

In conclusion, John Henry's life and legacy serve as a fascinating case study in the complex web of alliances and rivalries that shaped medieval Central Europe, and his continued influence on the politics and nobility of the region is a testament to the enduring power of medieval dynasties.

One striking statistic that highlights the significance of John Henry's reign is the fact that he was the father of Charles IV, Holy Roman Emperor, who went on to become one of the most important figures in medieval European history.
